Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our security/procurement side before we start the formal SIG: 

- HIPAA: we need confirmation that Redwood will sign a BAA and that PHI can be processed under the Dedicated offering (not hosted multi-tenant). Is Redwood currently accepting BAAs for Dedicated customers?
- SOC 2: do you have a Type II report (most recent period)? The summary is useful, but procurement will usually request the full report under an NDA.
- Data residency: Keystone requires US-only residency for the workload in scope. Will Dedicated nodes be provisioned in US-only hardware/regions and can you commit to that in the agreement?
- Technical asks: brief answers on key management (KMS/HSM), network segmentation, and SSO (SAML 2.0) would be helpful upfront.

We prefer SIG as the starting point. If you can prefill and attach the SOC 2 report under secure share (we will execute your NDA), that will speed procurement. Primary security contact: myself (evan.liu@keystonehealth.com). Procurement lead (legal): legal.procurement@keystonehealth.com.

Timeline: procurement is aiming to complete vendor review within 3 weeks, so early prefill helps a lot.

Marissa — quick answers you can paste into the prefill: 

1) BAA / HIPAA: YES — Redwood signs BAAs for Dedicated customers processing PHI. Standard practice: BAA commences once Dedicated environment is provisioned and the scope is defined. We typically include a limited data processing addendum; legal can provide a redline repo if procurement requests earlier.

2) SOC 2: We have a SOC 2 Type II report for the 2025 audit period. We do not publish the full report; we share it under NDA via secure share (link) or an in-person review room. Attached is the one-page SOC 2 summary (already in thread). For procurement, propose: (a) we send NDA and share report within 24 hours of execution, or (b) open a read-only share link to the report for Keystone's security review.

3) KMS/HSM, segmentation, SSO (short bullets):
- KMS/HSM: Customer keys supported via BYOK with cloud KMS integrations; HSM-backed key wrapping for Dedicated keys (AES-256 at rest).
- Network segmentation: Dedicated pools run in isolated VPCs with customer-configurable subnets and private peering; controls for egress whitelisting and VPC Flow logging.
- SSO: SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning supported for enterprise tenants; SSO can be enforced at tenant level.

4) Data residency: We can scope Dedicated nodes to US-only regions and document the residency commitment in the scope of work.

Notes for prefill: include the SOC 2 sharing path, mark BAA as "accepted for Dedicated in-scope environments", and add the three tech bullets above. I can jump on a short call with Keystone security if they want deeper detail.

—Ben
